# One analysis interface

Use `pca()`, `tsne()`, `umap()`, and `graph_cluster()` for both resident
and file-backed analysis. `massive_matrix()` describes a row-major
float32 file without loading it. A raw `.f32` file needs its row and
column counts; an `.fbin` file contains them in its header. Keep all
output paths on storage with sufficient space. These routes are
experimental and their supported backends differ.

Base R's `options()` can set session defaults for the backend, CPU workers,
storage preference, and file-backed working-memory budget. Explicit `backend`
and `memory_limit` arguments take precedence over their session defaults.
The public analysis functions also accept an explicit `storage` argument.
A storage choice that conflicts with the input is rejected.
`storage = "file_backed"` requires a disk-backed descriptor; it
never writes a resident matrix to disk implicitly.
The memory budget limits algorithm working buffers, not all process RSS or
GPU allocator overhead.
These ordinary R options can be shared by packages that use the same values;
restore the previous values when the analysis is finished.

```{r eval=FALSE}
old_options <- options(
  backend = "cpu", n.cores = 4L,
  storage = "file_backed",
  memory_limit = "8GB"
)
x <- massive_matrix("features.f32", nrow = 1000000L, ncol = 128L)
knn <- precompute_knn(x, k = 30L, output = "features-knn")
fuzzy <- massive_umap_fuzzy_graph(knn, output = "features-fuzzy",
                                 sort_method = "bucketed")
options(old_options)
```

For file-backed KNN, `precompute_knn()` returns a file-backed graph descriptor
rather than a resident `fastEmbedR_knn` object. It selects bounded exact or
sharded approximate search according to the backend and row count. Only
Euclidean distance is currently supported for this route. The output prefix
must be new and point to storage with enough free space. Convert the KNN
descriptor to a fuzzy graph or affinity graph before a full UMAP or t-SNE fit.
The fuzzy-graph conversion is currently a CPU step and also reads the session
memory budget when `memory_limit` is omitted. For t-SNE, use
`massive_tsne_affinities(knn, perplexity = 30, output = "features-affinity")`.

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(fastEmbedR)
x <- massive_matrix("features.f32", nrow = 1000000, ncol = 128)
fit_pca <- pca(x, ncomp = 30L, backend = "cpu",
               massive = "out_of_core",
               output = "scores.f32", memory_limit = "8GB")
first_scores <- massive_read_rows(fit_pca$scores, first = 1L, n = 6L)
```

`pca()` selects a memory-aware route for a file-backed descriptor when
`massive` is omitted. To require bounded block reads even when the
source is small, set `massive = "out_of_core"`. A large resident R matrix
is not silently converted to a file-backed source.

# Landmark embedding and clustering

For a file-backed matrix, set `landmarks` to a positive integer count to
request an approximate reference fit and fixed-reference projection.
Resident matrices also accept fractions and explicit row indices. This
changes the algorithm and should be reported with the result. A
persistent output path is required for file-backed inputs. A CPU,
Metal, or CUDA request either runs on that backend or fails explicitly.
Metal uses one Apple GPU; CUDA device support varies by route.

```{r eval=FALSE}
layout_u <- umap(x, landmarks = 10000L, backend = "cpu",
                 output = "umap.f32", memory_limit = "8GB")
layout_t <- tsne(x, landmarks = 10000L, backend = "cpu",
                 output = "tsne.f32", memory_limit = "8GB")
groups <- graph_cluster(x, method = "leiden", landmarks = 10000L,
                        backend = "cpu", output = "clusters",
                        memory_limit = "8GB")
head(massive_read_rows(groups))
```

For a resident matrix, the same calls use the ordinary resident route
when `landmarks` is absent. `graph_cluster()` accepts Leiden, Louvain,
and Walktrap. A landmark result assigns the remaining observations by
weighted voting; it is not full-data graph clustering.

# Full-graph analysis

A full file-backed fit requires a prepared nearest-neighbor graph.
Graph preparation is explicit because exact all-pairs search can take
quadratic time. The graph builders and importers remain public for
advanced use; the algorithm itself still runs through the four main
functions. The example below uses a bounded exact graph on a data size
where that search is practical.

```{r eval=FALSE}
small <- massive_matrix("small-features.f32", nrow = 2000L,
                        ncol = 128L)
knn <- precompute_knn(small, k = 30L, output = "full_knn",
                      backend = "cpu", memory_limit = "8GB")
fuzzy <- massive_umap_fuzzy_graph(knn, output = "fuzzy",
                                  sort_method = "bucketed")
initial <- massive_matrix("initial_2d.f32", nrow = small$nrow,
                          ncol = 2L)
layout <- umap(fuzzy, init = initial, output = "full_umap.f32",
               backend = "cpu", memory_limit = "8GB")
communities <- graph_cluster(fuzzy, method = "leiden",
                             output = "full_leiden",
                             backend = "cpu", memory_limit = "8GB")
```

The initialization must have one row per observation and two or three
columns. A full t-SNE fit uses an affinity graph from the same KNN
result, with a matching file-backed initialization:

```{r eval=FALSE}
affinity <- massive_tsne_affinities(
  knn, perplexity = 30, output = "full_affinity")
layout_t <- tsne(affinity, perplexity = 30, Y_init = initial,
                 output = "full_tsne.f32", backend = "cpu",
                 memory_limit = "8GB")
```

For file-backed full-graph fits, `umap()`, `tsne()`, and
`graph_cluster()` infer the route from the prepared graph. Specify
`massive = "out_of_core_graph"` when an explicit route is preferable.
Choose a file-backed graph and initialization appropriate to available
memory and storage. Neither `memory_limit` nor CUDA buffer estimates
are guarantees about total process RSS or GPU allocator overhead.

Checkpoint and resume controls are available for supported stages, but
recovery requires the same input files, backend, graph, and controls.
File-backed work should be run on a machine where SSD streaming is
permitted; the UCT HPC benchmark uses resident data only.
